messages:
ravi: Heads-up from a new-hire pairing session: the sample project README suggests setting RW_API_KEY but the quickstart container example sets RW_ORG_KEY. Folks then hit permission denied when they try to create project-scoped assets.
alex: Oof. Are those keys actually different shapes?
carmen: Yes — org keys start with org_ and can list/create projects; project keys start with proj_ and are limited to a single project. New hires copy the org key into RW_API_KEY env and then call the CLI with --project slugs and get 403s.
ravi: We should standardize on RW_API_KEY for interactive/local dev and RW_SERVICE_KEY for CI/deployments (org-scoped). Right now docs are inconsistent.
doc-bot: Reference: https://redwood.example/docs/auth#key-types (note: link is internal).
alex: Quick proposals: (1) update README + compose to only expose RW_API_KEY; (2) add a tiny startup check that validates the prefix of the provided key and warns if it doesn't match detected project config; (3) CLI `rw auth token-info` to show scope/prefix/expiry.
carmen: I like CLI token-info. Example output: ```
Type: project (proj_...)
Project: acme-payments
Expires: 2025-09-01T12:00:00Z
Effective scopes: read,write:models
```
ravi: SDK change idea: when a key mismatch is detected (project key used but CLI calls target org endpoints), surface a clear actionable error recommending which key to use. Could also suggest rw auth token-info in the error.
alex: Also add a small doc section on rotation: recommend rotating service/org keys in a staging environment first and how to roll project keys per-deployment.
devex-bot: Note: repeated support threads about 403s during onboarding; crosslinked tickets #5123 #5130.
carmen: I'll PR the README and add the token prefix check in the sample app entrypoint. @alex can you spec `rw auth token-info` and I'll file parity issues for node/python/go SDKs?
alex: On it, will add machine-readable JSON flag too for CI scripts.
ravi: Thanks — this should reduce a bunch of onboarding friction.
